object_description: two complementary building volumes around differentiated outdoor spaces
design_condition: Two new volumes are precisely arranged around the existing complex, with differentiated entrances and outdoor spaces mediating between the school and gymnasium while placing the main break area across the street.

positive.statement: The precise arrangement of the two new buildings creates a sequence of clearly assigned outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: The top view clearly shows two complementary masses with differentiated stepped outlines.

positive.statement: The differentiated entrances take account of the address formation of the individual uses.

position.rationale: Entrances are not distinct points, so a low-level street-facing edge is used.

positive.statement: The volumetric pivot mediates between the existing school complex and the new gymnasium building.

position.rationale: The central junction between staggered volumes is legible in the top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The access system cleverly separates the uses and connects them again via a second staircase and the elevator.

position.rationale: Stair and elevator routes are internal; the marker approximates the central circulation zone.

positive.statement: The ground-level arrangement and visual reference to the outside space are welcomed.

position.rationale: Repeated lower-level bands visibly define the ground-level organization.

positive.statement: The multi-purpose building impresses from a functional point of view, with a spacious foyer transitioning to the ground-level hall and viewing the outside space.

position.rationale: The foyer is internal and approximated within the lower portion of the principal volume.

positive.statement: Delivery is well organized at the rear of the facility.

position.rationale: Rear delivery is directionally constrained to the back perimeter visible in the top view.

positive.statement: The reserved appearance relates to the existing building and creates a unified whole.

position.rationale: Regular, restrained facade bands are visible across the elevations.

positive.statement: The buildings are simply structured and are expected to provide good profitability.

position.rationale: Profitability is a whole-building judgment without a specific spatial referent.

negative.statement: The break area being mainly on the other side of the street is viewed critically.

position.rationale: The external break area is not sampled; it is anchored beyond the rear site edge.

negative.statement: The kindergarten outdoor area seems somewhat tight, and information about its use and design is almost completely missing.

position.rationale: A constrained low-level edge zone represents the tight kindergarten exterior.

negative.statement: The access halls lack a connection to the outside and are not very suitable as learning zones.

position.rationale: Interior halls are not visible and are approximated within the central building depth.

negative.statement: The front glazing significantly impairs sports operations in the gymnasium.

position.rationale: The front elevation provides the strongest available facade anchor for the glazing critique.

negative.statement: The great depth of the school building could not be managed convincingly.

position.rationale: The top footprint and repeated deep elevation bands visibly support the depth assessment.

negative.statement: Defects in the lighting of the kindergartens and corridors and the introverted break halls are evidence of this.

position.rationale: Interior lighting conditions are unseen; the marker approximates a lower school zone.
